summary: Annotation search returns incomplete results and CSV export shows timestamp mismatch
description: Customer reports that when filtering dashboard annotations by tag and a time window, results are incomplete. Separately, exporting annotations to CSV returns records where timestamps are off by several hours (appears to be timezone/UTC drift) and some annotation metadata (user_id, trace_id) are missing. This impacts NoteForms' analytics and alert correlation between traces and annotation markers.
steps_to_reproduce: Open a dashboard with annotation layer that contains tags 'deploy' and 'monitor'.
Apply annotation filter: tag=deploy and time window last 7 days (relative).
Observe search results: only a subset of known deploy annotations are returned.
Click 'Export annotations' -> CSV and download file.
Inspect CSV: timestamps column shows values 4-8 hours earlier than dashboard hover timestamps; user_id and trace_id columns are often blank.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:22:05Z ERROR export-service: exportAnnotations: mismatch detected for annotation_id=ann-9f3a (created_at=2026-03-10T18:12:09Z, csv_timestamp=2026-03-10T14:12:09Z). request_id=req-7b21. filter_query=tag:deploy AND created_at:[2026-03-03 TO 2026-03-10].
investigation_notes: Initial triage: behavior reproduced in prod us-west by Support on 2026-03-10 at 14:30 UTC.
Hypothesis A: frontend applies local timezone conversion when rendering hover timestamps but export-service serializes timestamps in UTC without explicit tz label, causing perceived drift.
Hypothesis B: annotation indexer uses last_updated rather than created_at for search filters, causing older annotations to be excluded from relative time windows.
Checked indexer logs: occasional indexing lag observed for annotation writes during autoscale events (2026-03-09T02:00-02:15 UTC).
Trace correlation: missing trace_id in CSV corresponds to cases where user supplied trace pointer in annotation metadata; export pipeline strips nested metadata fields when flattening JSON->CSV.
customer_impact: NoteForms' analytics and automated alerts failed to correlate deploy markers with traces for ~12% of their recent annotations. They flagged this as impacting incident response and quarterly reporting.
workaround: Customer can use the Annotations API (v2) to fetch JSON payloads which include original created_at (with timezone) and full metadata. On frontend, avoid CSV exports until fix. Support provided a one-off JSON export for the last 30 days (S3 link sent).
resolution: Assigned to Console Backend (evan.brooks). Root causes: 1) export-service CSV serializer dropped nested fields by design; change requested to include user_id and trace_id columns. 2) search/filter pipeline used last_updated for relative ranges; updated to use created_at for annotation filter queries. 3) timestamps are now explicitly emitted in ISO 8601 with UTC offset. Hotfix deployed to staging 2026-03-12 and to prod 2026-03-12 22:10 UTC (release console@v2.18.4).
follow_up_actions: Create unit/integration tests for CSV serializer to preserve nested metadata (PR link in related_github_prs).
Add monitoring alert for annotation indexing lag > 2 minutes during autoscale windows.
Update export runbook with timezone guidance and add note in UI tooltip clarifying export timezone behavior.
